title: What AI Actually Is: Module Quiz

cards.prompt: Does each one **learn from examples**, or **follow rules** someone wrote?

items.label: An online shop's "you might like" list

cards.explanation: A microwave timer and spreadsheet sums follow exact rules. Speech to text and "you might like" lists face endless variety, so they **learn from examples**.
Every basketball it learned from was big, so the mini one sat nearer the tennis balls. Adding the **small basketball** fixes it; another big basketball or tennis ball doesn't.

cards.prompt: A dog spotter learned only from **daylight** photos. What will it most likely get wrong?

options.text: The photos it was trained on
Dogs in photos taken at night
Nothing: the kind of photos doesn't matter

cards.explanation: It never saw a dog at night, so night photos are where it will slip up, like the yellow apple. Adding night photos would help.

cards.prompt: A café trained a burnt-toast spotter on labelled photos, used it at once, and it calls dark rye burnt. Why?

options.text: They skipped trying it on new toast before using it
They should have used it before labelling photos
Labels confused it: unlabelled photos work better
Rye is too dark: testing first wouldn't have helped

cards.explanation: The steps are collect, label, train, **test on new examples**, then use. Testing on darker breads would have caught the mistake before customers did.

cards.prompt: You're writing quiz-night questions with an AI helper.

steps.text: The AI confidently names the world's highest volcano. Teams will argue every answer. What do you do?

choices.consequence: It might be right or not. AI answers are predictions, however confident.

choices.text: Check it in a trusted source first
choices.consequence: Exactly: important facts get checked with a source you trust.

choices.text: Ask the AI to promise it's right
choices.consequence: It may promise, but it can't be sure its own answer is right.

cards.explanation: An AI's answer is a prediction. For anything important, **check it with a trusted source** before you rely on it.

cards.prompt: A company uses AI to sort 500 job applications. Who should make the final call?

options.text: A person who checks the AI's picks and is responsible
The AI, because it's faster and never gets tired
A manager who simply hires whoever the AI picks
The AI, as it learned from thousands of past hires

cards.explanation: Jobs are a **big decision about people**. AI picks are predictions, so a person checks them, decides and is responsible. Rubber-stamping the AI isn't deciding.

cards.prompt: A cats-and-dogs photo sorter: match each part to its word.

pairs.left: The program that sorts new photos
"Dog": its guess for a new photo

cards.explanation: The photos are **training data**, "cat" on one photo is a **label**, the sorting program is the **model**, and its guess is a **prediction**.
